SECRET SUNRISE

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
…dancing to daylight at a secret location is the latest urban craze to leap into reality from social media… We go underground to find out what Secret Sunrise is all about.

Summary:
Each day, dawns with new amazing possibilities, with the potential for us to really embrace this human experience. So why not get up early, immerse ourselves in the beauty of our city and let go as we dance and celebrate for no reason at all?

Secret Sunrise a new movement that starts on Facebook and brings together a group of diverse sunrisers in an early morning interactive SILENT dance session. It is a fun, energetic celebration that combines yoga, meditation, make believe and dancing.

It’s young, it’s fresh and it’s going global!


Further information:
The SECRET SUNRISE event is posted online, but the location is only revealed 24 hours before.

It’s all very exciting - waking up before dawn and migrating to secret locations where people dance until sunrise. The core philosophy is "Share the Joy.

These sessions are a perfect platform to help people to feel free, to express themselves and to reap the benefits of letting go.

All the ‘Sunrisers’ have to do is let go and enjoy.

HOW WE DO IT
We take a presenter to next event – next week Wednesday (ideally we get them to dress up a bit to, I thought maybe Devi could do the story as she loves yoga and I think would be game to wear a tutu for a bit ☺ )

We cover the class, and follow two regulars – an investment banker and an IT manager – showing how they transform from straight laced office bounded career driven people to letting go in quirky outfits in unusual settings dancing in the day.

The serious element comes through a Drama Therapist who explains the value of a movement like this.

A PARTY WITHOUT NOISE AND DRUG AND BOOZE?!?!?!?
YES! It’s actually NOT a dance party. The organisers promote healthy living. No drugs or alcohol is permitted! Instead, health smoothies, circle dancing and superhero costumes are all part of the fun.

DRESS UP IS PART OF THE GAME
Dress up is optional but highly recommended - be as silly as possible!

Some 300 people dance in silence, some dressed as Batman, Spiderman or Wonder Woman. Others are in tutus, black catsuits or animal "onesies". Many have masks and painted faces.
At Secret Sunrise they like to celebrate the unordinary and step out of our comfort zones. It’s a great opportunity to let go in a safe space, be ridiculous and have some fun.
The themed sessions although fun and quirky also offer us the opportunity to explore and delve into deeper and more mindful topics, such as compassion, self-expression, fear and acceptance.

THE ART OF A SILENT DISCO
The event has little noise pollution due to the headphones. Guests are given wireless headphones on arrival and the whacky instructors guide them through a unique, themed session. The special headphones pump out a DJs playlist, giving the guests the beats they need to dance, without waking up the neighbours.

The sessions are hosted in interesting and unique spaces like roof tops, train stations and golf courses – the team behind strive to find the perfect sunrise.
JAMIE BERON - ORGANISER
"It is an opportunity to go wild, to be ridiculous,"
31 year old Jamie Beron is one of the organisers of the fortnightly event. He’s also a yoga teacher and embraces secret sunrises donning leopard-print leggings, fishnet gloves and a very tight silver shirt
THE VISION
The hope is that Secret Sunrise will bring people together and will help us to start to engender a greater community spirit. They firmly believe that these sessions will help to cultivate change. By breaking down preconceptions and by pushing people out of their comfort zones a little we are helping our beautiful 'Sunrisers' to experience a greater sense of freedom and connectedness and hopefully a vast array of emotions too. Come and sing, dance, laugh, cry, shout, stomp, hug and find stillness all in a safe space where these emotions are not only accepted but encouraged.

IT’S TAKING OFF!
It started off as a quirky event in Jozi, but now has movements in Cape Town, Durban, Stellenbosch and Pretoria with the international dance community getting curious about this new adventure with a London event in the planning stages.

IT’s NOT JUST A HIPPIE FEST – IT’s THERAPEUTIC
SIAN PALMER – EXPERT / DRAMA THERAPIST
Sian has a Masters Degree in Drama and Movement from the University of London. She says Secret Sunrise is an embodiment of Drama Therapy. It takes on a safe, non-judgemental and non-confrontational approach using the mediums of drama and movement as a means of facilitating the potential for growth and healing.
It is not about performing or being good at dance. The emphasis is less on talking and more on using the imagination and body. Dramatherapy facilitates a space for individuals to discover the ability that lies within to be creative and playful.

WHO ARE SECRET SUNRISERS?
It’s for everyone. There’s no age limitations, it does not matter if you are fit, unfit, courageous or shy. The aim is to make this movement as inclusive and accessible as possible.

We hook up with two regulars - Investment Banker - Jo Maharaj and IT project Manager Burgher Nortje who forget their corporate personas while dancing in the daylight, proudly embracing a less reserved way to live for an hour every two weeks.
TYPES OF COMMENTS FROM OTHER CASE STUDIES:
Cheryl Hudson: Works in project finance when she changes out of her purple dance outfit.
"You get to be a different version of yourself, you go forth, and you are not grumpy when you get into the office. As adults, we sometimes forget... that we really need to play.”
Travis Kruger: Transforms from a sweaty Captain America to a used-car salesman during work hours.
"You can dance where no one cares if you can dance. Everyone is just happy and free and you get to hug people. You don't have to say any word to anyone. I have to go to work after this. Last time I did this, I had the most amazing day at work, so it is just a good start to the day."

Press Release:


Secret Sunrise
The straight-laced investor or sales guy in the nearby work station could have spent a couple of hours before work dancing at dawn, out in the open, and you’d never know it! The latest urban craze to leap from social media into reality sees free spirits gather on city rooftops in secret locations for a kaleidoscope of movement and colour where anything goes. Carte Blanche exposes the sunrise’s best kept secret.


Script:


STRUCTURE SECRET SUNRISE

VO: We live in a world where we are constantly connected through social media, yet this virtual connectivity often lacks physical interaction.

But a new urban craze is taking hundreds of strangers out of Facebook’s cyber world, to a real world out in the open.

JAMIE: So much of life is expected, so much is routine. We are going to wake up, we are going to eat our cornflakes, we are going to go work. // It’s so nice to offer a little of intrigue, a little bit of mystery into people’s lives.

VO: Secret Sunrise is a movement that started in Cape Town, and has spread to Jo’burg, Pretoria and Durban with almost 11 000 fans on Facebook.

The location and theme for the event is only revealed 24 hours before – keeping the element of surprise says organiser Jamie Beron.

JAMIE: It’s not about image and looking cool. It’s a party that helps you experience a little bit of energy and do some exercise at the same time.

VO: You get up at the crack of dawn, drive to the secret location and then, you dance in the daylight.

SIAN: It’s then moving beyond the technology back to connecting // to return to the very primitive practice of dance and celebration.

VO: Dancing in the daylight is a fast growing international trend. And Secret Sunrise is South Africa’s twist to the mix - combining yoga, meditation, dance and a bit intrigue… the magic starts at 6 am and lasts for an hour.

It’s an opportunity to be free, to be wild and purposefully ridiculous without any booze or drugs.

LINK: It’s completely bizarre, because all you can hear is the traffic at Hyde Park Corner, then you put this on and you enter a whole other world.

VO: The music is contained in wireless headsets that operate on radio frequencies. A specifically chosen playlist is pumped to the headphones, giving the Sunrisers the beats to move to, without waking up the neighbourhood.

But who are these so-called sunrisers? Just a bunch of hippies? Nope! This movement has got everyone going with all sorts in the crowd.

EBEN KILIAN, WOOD FURNITURE ENTREPRENEUR – your average guy.

EBEN: I don’t think I’m the yoga, dancing type. // it’s a different morning

VO: JO MAHARAJ, INVESTMENT BANKER – a high-flying corporate type

JO: we’re multi dimensional people and we just want to explore ourselves in every aspect

VO: BURGHER NORTJE, - IT PROJECT MANAGER – your new-age computer dude.

BURGHER: You get to go be a kid again without any preconceived judgments or expectations

VO: Drama and Movement Therapist Sian Palmer says despite the seemingly crazy chaos, this is a form of meditation that allows a chattery mind to find focus through movement.

SIAN: It’s done in community through the medium of dance.
DEVI: Most people would never look at that and think it’s meditation is Budha sitting. How is this meditation?
SIAN: Dance encourages you to engage your senses // It really is about going into the body and becoming present. // and then responding to what you discover while you are there, so it really is an active meditation that enables you to move moment by moment.

LINK: It’s a completely type of different exercise, you’ve got clowns, you’ve got leopard print, you’ve got tutus, you’ve got just about everything, and these people still have to get to work, because it is the middle of working week.

CHERYL: // Starting your day like this and going into an office, you literally can’t have a bad day. So it’s a nice way to transform the daily grind, and break down the barriers you usually come into work with.

VO: Cheryl Hudson is also one of the organisers. You might think she lives a double life - because most days Cheryl is a Renewable Energies Project Financier at a big Corporate Bank.

CHERYL: I like to think of it as exploring a different side of me. Secret Sunrise for me is a beautiful space where I can explore some creativity.

VO: Eben Kilian runs his own wood furniture store. While he works out regularly, he say it can become monotonous.

EBEN: With gym in the morning you go with a clear intention in the morning, knowing exactly what you are going to do – this is completely unknown/

VO: Co-organiser Jamie left the film industry to explore a career as a yoga teacher. He says the beauty of Secret Sunrise is that it’s for everyone.

JAMIE: You really never have to ever have been on a yoga mat. // we pride ourselves on the fact that we are probably terrible at dancing, we just like to move, we like to let go

VO: Burgher Nortje is an IT Project Manager – with most of his day scheduled down to the minute he loves the element of surprise.

BURGHER: I’m not really an adrenalin junkie wanting to jump off buildings and tall bridges and stuff doesn’t necessarily appeal to me but being to explore my personality and character that’s what appealed to me ultimately

VO: The investment banker in Jo Maharaj, believes the success goes beyond the conventional supply vs demand strategy.

JO: Sometimes the best ideas are not dictated by finding demand in people that is unmet – it is actually by creating demand in people for something that is different. And I love the ingenuity of that.

VO: And there is real value in good vibes - Sian says studies have shown that exploring one’s creativity can foster healthy living.

SIAN: your body is your vehicle – it’s what navigates you from A-B, so the stronger and the more in tune you are with your body, the more you can engage with the world.

VO: Ultimately, these sessions aim to go beyond just silly dance moves.

JAMIE: The first thing we help people relax. And we do that by means of some breathing work, some yoga.
BURGHER: // the precursor to all of the madness is the narration just telling you to enjoy yourself, let yourself go, let your limbs shake loose,

VO: The sessions then kicks up a notched with instructor lead dance – it usually comes as a surprise for newbies, as Eben recalls his first time.

EBEN: I stood there not really knowing what was going on,// it is self-conscious in the beginning, but everybody just does their own thing and you can see people just relaxing and enjoying it. So there’s no reason for you not to.

VO: And as the hour wraps up, the session takes a more reflective tone.

JAMIE: //The theme is always chosen so we can communicate a deeper more conscious message. // to make these events a little bit more than just a get together and a dance, //

VO: For Jo, Secret Sunrise is just an extension of her creative self.

JO: We have a silly assumption that progress is linear, success is binary, we’ve got all these ideas in our head, and I don’t see the jucture position in myself, as someone who would go to secret sunrise and by day I am an investment banker. //

VO: While dress up is not essential, it’s encouraged and adds to the adventure says IT man Burgher.

BURGHER: I love it! // You will see someone who might not be as radical, but there will always be someone who is far more radical and completely in character and having a ball of a time.
DEVI: Is it worth getting up at dawn?
BURGHER: // after it all you’re actually pumped up, you’re high on life
EBEN: you’re more energised, you’re more open to suggestions, you’re more focussed on what you need to do.
JO: Imagine dancing in your room to some music before you go to work, and take that feeling and times it by 10 million.

BURGHER: I’m not really an adrenalin junkie wanting to jump off buildings and tall bridges and stuff doesn’t necessarily appeal to me but being to explore my personality and character that’s what appealed to me ultimately VO: The investment banker in Jo Maharaj, believes the success goes beyond the conventional supply vs demand strategy. JO: Sometimes the best ideas are not dictated by finding demand in people that is unmet – it is actually by creating demand in people for something that is different. And I love the ingenuity of that. VO: And there is real value in good vibes - Sian says studies have shown that exploring one’s creativity can foster healthy living. SIAN: your body is your vehicle – it’s what navigates you from A-B, so the stronger and the more in tune you are with your body, the more you can engage with the world. VO: Ultimately, these sessions aim to go beyond just silly dance moves. JAMIE: The first thing we help people relax. And we do that by means of some breathing work, some yoga. BURGHER: // the precursor to all of the madness is the narration just telling you to enjoy yourself, let yourself go, let your limbs shake loose, VO: The sessions then kicks up a notched with instructor lead dance – it usually comes as a surprise for newbies, as Eben recalls his first time. EBEN: I stood there not really knowing what was going on,// it is self-conscious in the beginning, but everybody just does their own thing and you can see people just relaxing and enjoying it. So there’s no reason for you not to. VO: And as the hour wraps up, the session takes a more reflective tone. JAMIE: //The theme is always chosen so we can communicate a deeper more conscious message. // to make these events a little bit more than just a get together and a dance, // VO: For Jo, Secret Sunrise is just an extension of her creative self. JO: We have a silly assumption that progress is linear, success is binary, we’ve got all these ideas in our head, and I don’t see the jucture position in myself, as someone who would go to secret sunrise and by day I am an investment banker. // VO: While dress up is not essential, it’s encouraged and adds to the adventure says IT man Burgher. BURGHER: I love it! // You will see someone who might not be as radical, but there will always be someone who is far more radical and completely in character and having a ball of a time. DEVI: Is it worth getting up at dawn? BURGHER: // after it all you’re actually pumped up, you’re high on life EBEN: you’re more energised, you’re more open to suggestions, you’re more focussed on what you need to do. JO: Imagine dancing in your room to some music before you go to work, and take that feeling and times it by 10 million. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): …dancing to daylight at a secret location is the latest urban craze to leap into reality from social media… We go underground to find out what Secret Sunrise is all about.
metadata.Summary: Each day, dawns with new amazing possibilities, with the potential for us to really embrace this human experience. So why not get up early, immerse ourselves in the beauty of our city and let go as we dance and celebrate for no reason at all? Secret Sunrise a new movement that starts on Facebook and brings together a group of diverse sunrisers in an early morning interactive SILENT dance session. It is a fun, energetic celebration that combines yoga, meditation, make believe and dancing. It’s young, it’s fresh and it’s going global!
metadata.Further information: The SECRET SUNRISE event is posted online, but the location is only revealed 24 hours before. It’s all very exciting - waking up before dawn and migrating to secret locations where people dance until sunrise. The core philosophy is "Share the Joy. These sessions are a perfect platform to help people to feel free, to express themselves and to reap the benefits of letting go. All the ‘Sunrisers’ have to do is let go and enjoy. HOW WE DO IT We take a presenter to next event – next week Wednesday (ideally we get them to dress up a bit to, I thought maybe Devi could do the story as she loves yoga and I think would be game to wear a tutu for a bit ☺ ) We cover the class, and follow two regulars – an investment banker and an IT manager – showing how they transform from straight laced office bounded career driven people to letting go in quirky outfits in unusual settings dancing in the day. The serious element comes through a Drama Therapist who explains the value of a movement like this. A PARTY WITHOUT NOISE AND DRUG AND BOOZE?!?!?!? YES! It’s actually NOT a dance party. The organisers promote healthy living. No drugs or alcohol is permitted! Instead, health smoothies, circle dancing and superhero costumes are all part of the fun. DRESS UP IS PART OF THE GAME Dress up is optional but highly recommended - be as silly as possible! Some 300 people dance in silence, some dressed as Batman, Spiderman or Wonder Woman. Others are in tutus, black catsuits or animal "onesies". Many have masks and painted faces. At Secret Sunrise they like to celebrate the unordinary and step out of our comfort zones. It’s a great opportunity to let go in a safe space, be ridiculous and have some fun. The themed sessions although fun and quirky also offer us the opportunity to explore and delve into deeper and more mindful topics, such as compassion, self-expression, fear and acceptance. THE ART OF A SILENT DISCO The event has little noise pollution due to the headphones. Guests are given wireless headphones on arrival and the whacky instructors guide them through a unique, themed session. The special headphones pump out a DJs playlist, giving the guests the beats they need to dance, without waking up the neighbours. The sessions are hosted in interesting and unique spaces like roof tops, train stations and golf courses – the team behind strive to find the perfect sunrise. JAMIE BERON - ORGANISER "It is an opportunity to go wild, to be ridiculous," 31 year old Jamie Beron is one of the organisers of the fortnightly event. He’s also a yoga teacher and embraces secret sunrises donning leopard-print leggings, fishnet gloves and a very tight silver shirt THE VISION The hope is that Secret Sunrise will bring people together and will help us to start to engender a greater community spirit. They firmly believe that these sessions will help to cultivate change. By breaking down preconceptions and by pushing people out of their comfort zones a little we are helping our beautiful 'Sunrisers' to experience a greater sense of freedom and connectedness and hopefully a vast array of emotions too. Come and sing, dance, laugh, cry, shout, stomp, hug and find stillness all in a safe space where these emotions are not only accepted but encouraged. IT’S TAKING OFF! It started off as a quirky event in Jozi, but now has movements in Cape Town, Durban, Stellenbosch and Pretoria with the international dance community getting curious about this new adventure with a London event in the planning stages. IT’s NOT JUST A HIPPIE FEST – IT’s THERAPEUTIC SIAN PALMER – EXPERT / DRAMA THERAPIST Sian has a Masters Degree in Drama and Movement from the University of London. She says Secret Sunrise is an embodiment of Drama Therapy. It takes on a safe, non-judgemental and non-confrontational approach using the mediums of drama and movement as a means of facilitating the potential for growth and healing. It is not about performing or being good at dance. The emphasis is less on talking and more on using the imagination and body. Dramatherapy facilitates a space for individuals to discover the ability that lies within to be creative and playful. WHO ARE SECRET SUNRISERS? It’s for everyone. There’s no age limitations, it does not matter if you are fit, unfit, courageous or shy. The aim is to make this movement as inclusive and accessible as possible. We hook up with two regulars - Investment Banker - Jo Maharaj and IT project Manager Burgher Nortje who forget their corporate personas while dancing in the daylight, proudly embracing a less reserved way to live for an hour every two weeks. TYPES OF COMMENTS FROM OTHER CASE STUDIES: Cheryl Hudson: Works in project finance when she changes out of her purple dance outfit. "You get to be a different version of yourself, you go forth, and you are not grumpy when you get into the office. As adults, we sometimes forget... that we really need to play.” Travis Kruger: Transforms from a sweaty Captain America to a used-car salesman during work hours. "You can dance where no one cares if you can dance. Everyone is just happy and free and you get to hug people. You don't have to say any word to anyone. I have to go to work after this. Last time I did this, I had the most amazing day at work, so it is just a good start to the day."
